card.title: Short Circuits - Repair Basics

claims.statement: Confirm a short with the black probe on ground (diode or resistance mode); reversed probes can read low through IC protection diodes. CPU/GPU core rails can legitimately read 0–1 Ω.

Locate shorts by visual inspection first, then feeling for hot parts, then voltage injection (start at about 1 V, never above the rail's rated voltage/current) with a thermal camera, freeze spray or IPA.
If nothing heats, the short may be very low impedance (solder bridge, MOSFET, diode, big cap) or on a rail derived from the suspect rail; recheck after removing any jumpers.
Supplies protect against shorts via series resistors, fuses (incl. polyfuses) or active current limiting; supplies that shut off and retry cause 'clicking'/cycling voltage.

procedure: Measure rail to ground with black probe on ground.
Power up briefly and feel for hot parts.
Inject ~1 V and use thermal camera / freeze spray / IPA.
Remove the hot part and re-measure.

measurements.context: Safe starting point for most rails

card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
